WUM-001.scenario: Verify that the Roles tab lists the base roles
WUM-001.preconditions: Admin is signed in. Note: User Management is still under development, so a failure here is pending development, not a defect.
steps: Open User Management.
Click the Roles tab and wait for it to load.
Look for the base role names on the page.
WUM-001.test_data: Base roles: Admin, Customer, Business, Operations
WUM-001.expected: At least one of the base roles (Admin, Customer, Business, Operations) is listed.

WUM-002.scenario: Verify that an admin can create a new role and set its module access
WUM-002.preconditions: Admin is signed in. User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management and click the Roles tab.
Click New role.
Enter a role name and description.
In the access table, set Beneficiary to View (if the table is available).
Click Save.
WUM-002.test_data: Role name: 'QA_' + 5 random capital letters (e.g. QA_KXRTM); description: a short random sentence; Beneficiary access: View
WUM-002.expected: A confirmation message appears or the new role is shown in the roles list.

WUM-004.scenario: Check that the Admin and Customer base roles cannot be deleted
WUM-004.preconditions: Admin is signed in. The role row must exist (otherwise skipped). User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management and click the Roles tab.
Find the row for the base role.
Look for a Delete button in that row.
WUM-004.expected: The role has no Delete button, or the Delete button is disabled.

WUM-006.scenario: Verify that the Invite New User form shows the Email, Full Name and Contact Number fields
WUM-006.preconditions: Admin is signed in. User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management and click the Users tab.
Click Add User.
Check the fields on the form.
WUM-006.expected: The form has Email, Full Name and Contact Number fields.

WUM-007.scenario: Verify that an admin can invite a new user with a role and hierarchy level
WUM-007.preconditions: Admin is signed in. User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management and click the Users tab.
Click Add User.
Enter Email, Full Name and Contact Number.
Choose the role Operations and the hierarchy level Maker (if available).
Click Send Invitation.
WUM-007.test_data: Email: a generated test address starting 'qa.user'; Full Name: a random name; Contact: a random 10-digit mobile; Role: Operations; Hierarchy: Maker
WUM-007.expected: A confirmation message appears or the invited user is shown in the users list.

WUM-008.scenario: Check that the invite is blocked when the contact number is not exactly 10 digits
WUM-008.preconditions: Admin is signed in. User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management, click the Users tab, then Add User.
Enter a valid Email and Full Name, and an invalid Contact Number.
Click Send Invitation.
Check whether the form is still open.
WUM-008.expected: The invite is not sent; the form stays open with the Contact Number field shown.

WUM-009.scenario: Verify that choosing the Customer role shows the Assigned Virtual ID field
WUM-009.preconditions: Admin is signed in. User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management, click the Users tab, then Add User.
Open the Role list and choose Customer.
Look for the Assigned Virtual ID field.
WUM-009.expected: The Assigned Virtual ID field appears on the form.

WUM-014.scenario: Check that script code typed into Full Name is not run by the browser
WUM-014.preconditions: Admin is signed in. User Management is still under development.
steps: Open User Management, click the Users tab, then Add User.
Enter a valid Email and Contact Number, and the script text in Full Name.
Click Send Invitation.
Watch for any pop-up alert box.
WUM-014.expected: No pop-up alert appears; the script text is not executed.
